input.quote: a. it will perform the Services using reasonable care and skill and in accordance with the applicable Service Option Attachments
input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services performance warranty (reasonable care and skill, roughly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) and a compliance-with-laws covenant, but there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no warranty period, and no remedy anywhere in the agreement (no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund; no SLA or credits). Worse, Section 5.4(c) provides all Materials — including Type I Materials created for Customer — "AS IS" without warranty of any kind, so the disclaimer swallows any deliverable-level assurance. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with the stated remedies) and approaches the walk-away position. Our redline sits at the fallback: a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, plus an "except as expressly warranted" carve-out in the AS IS disclaimer.

ops.text: c. for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable and the Materials will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and specifications, and the Materials will not contain any virus, worm or other malicious code. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Deliverable or Materials, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services, Deliverable or Materials.

ops.oldText: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES
ops.newText: c. Except as expressly warranted in Section 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables and Materials with a re-performance/repair/refund remedy, plus a no-malicious-code assurance, and carved the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer so it does not swallow them. Our playbook requires a real conformance warranty and remedy; 90 days is our fallback position, and we are happy to discuss the mechanics.
proposal.summary: Add 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with repair/replace/refund remedy and carve express warranties out of the AS IS disclaimer.
